claims.title: Mission of Cyril and Methodius to Great Moravia
claims.summary: At the request of Prince Rostislav, the Byzantine brothers Cyril and Methodius came to Great Moravia, translated the liturgy into Old Church Slavonic and devised the Glagolitic alphabet, bringing Christianity to the Slavs.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Czechia: From Great Moravia and the crown of Saint Wenceslas to the heart of Europe, by way of Hus, White Mountain and two peaceful revolutions.", terralore.co/country/CZE/chronicle#ev-863-mission-of-cyril-and-methodius-to-great-moravia, claim TL:CZE:event:863:mission-of-cyril-and-methodius-to-great-moravia, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Fall of Great Moravia
claims.summary: Weakened by internal division and overwhelmed by the Magyars, Great Moravia disintegrated in the early tenth century, and leadership of the western Slavs shifted to the Premyslid dukes of Bohemia.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Czechia: From Great Moravia and the crown of Saint Wenceslas to the heart of Europe, by way of Hus, White Mountain and two peaceful revolutions.", terralore.co/country/CZE/chronicle#ev-907-fall-of-great-moravia, claim TL:CZE:event:907:fall-of-great-moravia, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Martyrdom of Saint Wenceslas
claims.summary: Wenceslas (Vaclav), Premyslid duke of Bohemia and promoter of Christianity, was murdered by his brother and was at once venerated as a martyr, becoming the patron saint of the Czech nation.

sources.label: Wenceslas I, prince of Bohemia (Saint Wenceslas)

claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Czechia: From Great Moravia and the crown of Saint Wenceslas to the heart of Europe, by way of Hus, White Mountain and two peaceful revolutions.", terralore.co/country/CZE/chronicle#ev-929-martyrdom-of-saint-wenceslas, claim TL:CZE:event:929:martyrdom-of-saint-wenceslas, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Golden Bull of Sicily and the Kingdom of Bohemia
claims.summary: The Golden Bull of Sicily, issued by Emperor Frederick II, confirmed the royal title of the Premyslid rulers as hereditary, formally raising Bohemia from a duchy to a kingdom within the Holy Roman Empire.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Czechia: From Great Moravia and the crown of Saint Wenceslas to the heart of Europe, by way of Hus, White Mountain and two peaceful revolutions.", terralore.co/country/CZE/chronicle#ev-1212-golden-bull-of-sicily-and-the-kingdom-of-bohemia, claim TL:CZE:event:1212:golden-bull-of-sicily-and-the-kingdom-of-bohemia, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: End of the Premyslid dynasty
claims.summary: The murder of Wenceslas III extinguished the male line of the Premyslids; after a brief contest the Bohemian crown passed to the House of Luxembourg, the dynasty of Charles IV.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Czechia: From Great Moravia and the crown of Saint Wenceslas to the heart of Europe, by way of Hus, White Mountain and two peaceful revolutions.", terralore.co/country/CZE/chronicle#ev-1306-end-of-the-premyslid-dynasty, claim TL:CZE:event:1306:end-of-the-premyslid-dynasty, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Foundation of Charles University
claims.summary: Charles IV founded the university in Prague that bears his name, the first university in central Europe, endowed with the same rights and liberties as the universities of Paris and Bologna.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Czechia: From Great Moravia and the crown of Saint Wenceslas to the heart of Europe, by way of Hus, White Mountain and two peaceful revolutions.", terralore.co/country/CZE/chronicle#ev-1348-foundation-of-charles-university, claim TL:CZE:event:1348:foundation-of-charles-university, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Charles IV crowned Holy Roman Emperor
claims.summary: Already king of Bohemia, Charles was crowned Holy Roman Emperor in Rome in 1355, making Prague the principal residence of the Empire and the centre of European politics and culture.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Czechia: From Great Moravia and the crown of Saint Wenceslas to the heart of Europe, by way of Hus, White Mountain and two peaceful revolutions.", terralore.co/country/CZE/chronicle#ev-1355-charles-iv-crowned-holy-roman-emperor, claim TL:CZE:event:1355:charles-iv-crowned-holy-roman-emperor, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Building of Charles Bridge and Gothic Prague
claims.summary: Charles IV laid the foundation of the stone bridge over the Vltava and advanced St Vitus Cathedral and the New Town, creating the Gothic core of Prague later recognised as a UNESCO World Heritage site.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Czechia: From Great Moravia and the crown of Saint Wenceslas to the heart of Europe, by way of Hus, White Mountain and two peaceful revolutions.", terralore.co/country/CZE/chronicle#ev-1357-building-of-charles-bridge-and-gothic-prague, claim TL:CZE:event:1357:building-of-charles-bridge-and-gothic-prague, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Jan Hus preaches at the Bethlehem Chapel
claims.summary: Appointed preacher at the Bethlehem Chapel in Prague, Hus began to denounce church corruption and indulgences and to champion reform and vernacular preaching, drawing on the ideas of John Wycliffe.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Czechia: From Great Moravia and the crown of Saint Wenceslas to the heart of Europe, by way of Hus, White Mountain and two peaceful revolutions.", terralore.co/country/CZE/chronicle#ev-1402-jan-hus-preaches-at-the-bethlehem-chapel, claim TL:CZE:event:1402:jan-hus-preaches-at-the-bethlehem-chapel, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Jan Hus burned at the Council of Constance
claims.summary: Condemned as a heretic despite a promise of safe conduct, Hus was burned at the stake at Constance on 6 July 1415, becoming a martyr whose death set off the Hussite movement.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Czechia: From Great Moravia and the crown of Saint Wenceslas to the heart of Europe, by way of Hus, White Mountain and two peaceful revolutions.", terralore.co/country/CZE/chronicle#ev-1415-jan-hus-burned-at-the-council-of-constance, claim TL:CZE:event:1415:jan-hus-burned-at-the-council-of-constance, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: The Hussite Wars
claims.summary: Followers of Hus fought a series of wars against the Catholic crown and papal crusades; under Jan Zizka the Hussite armies proved nearly invincible before the conflict ended in compromise.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Czechia: From Great Moravia and the crown of Saint Wenceslas to the heart of Europe, by way of Hus, White Mountain and two peaceful revolutions.", terralore.co/country/CZE/chronicle#ev-1419-the-hussite-wars, claim TL:CZE:event:1419:the-hussite-wars, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Compact of Iglau
claims.summary: The moderate Utraquist Hussites secured a peace settlement, the Compact of Iglau, that granted communion in both kinds and an independent Bohemian Catholic church, ending the main phase of the wars.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Czechia: From Great Moravia and the crown of Saint Wenceslas to the heart of Europe, by way of Hus, White Mountain and two peaceful revolutions.", terralore.co/country/CZE/chronicle#ev-1436-compact-of-iglau, claim TL:CZE:event:1436:compact-of-iglau, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Bohemia under the Habsburgs
claims.summary: The Bohemian estates elected Ferdinand I of Habsburg as king, binding the kingdom to the Habsburg monarchy and to Austria and Hungary for nearly four centuries.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Czechia: From Great Moravia and the crown of Saint Wenceslas to the heart of Europe, by way of Hus, White Mountain and two peaceful revolutions.", terralore.co/country/CZE/chronicle#ev-1526-bohemia-under-the-habsburgs, claim TL:CZE:event:1526:bohemia-under-the-habsburgs, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Defenestration of Prague
claims.summary: Protestant nobles threw two Catholic imperial regents and their secretary from a window of Prague Castle, sparking the Bohemian revolt against Ferdinand II and helping to launch the Thirty Years' War.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Czechia: From Great Moravia and the crown of Saint Wenceslas to the heart of Europe, by way of Hus, White Mountain and two peaceful revolutions.", terralore.co/country/CZE/chronicle#ev-1618-defenestration-of-prague, claim TL:CZE:event:1618:defenestration-of-prague, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Battle of White Mountain
claims.summary: Imperial and Catholic League armies crushed the Bohemian rebels at White Mountain near Prague, ending Czech estates' power and ushering in Habsburg absolutism and forced Counter-Reformation.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Czechia: From Great Moravia and the crown of Saint Wenceslas to the heart of Europe, by way of Hus, White Mountain and two peaceful revolutions.", terralore.co/country/CZE/chronicle#ev-1620-battle-of-white-mountain, claim TL:CZE:event:1620:battle-of-white-mountain, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: The Czech National Revival
claims.summary: From the late 18th century, scholars led by the historian Frantisek Palacky rebuilt and codified the Czech language and national history, transforming a cultural awakening into a political movement within Austria-Hungary.

sources.label: Czechoslovak history: National awakening and the rise of constitutionalism

claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Czechia: From Great Moravia and the crown of Saint Wenceslas to the heart of Europe, by way of Hus, White Mountain and two peaceful revolutions.", terralore.co/country/CZE/chronicle#ev-1848-the-czech-national-revival, claim TL:CZE:event:1848:the-czech-national-revival, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Foundation of Czechoslovakia
claims.summary: With Austria-Hungary collapsing, independence was proclaimed in Prague on 28 October 1918; Tomas Garrigue Masaryk became the first president of the new multi-ethnic democratic republic.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Czechia: From Great Moravia and the crown of Saint Wenceslas to the heart of Europe, by way of Hus, White Mountain and two peaceful revolutions.", terralore.co/country/CZE/chronicle#ev-1918-foundation-of-czechoslovakia, claim TL:CZE:event:1918:foundation-of-czechoslovakia, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: The Munich Agreement
claims.summary: Germany, Italy, Britain and France agreed at Munich that Czechoslovakia must cede the German-majority Sudetenland to Nazi Germany; Czechoslovakia was not a party and yielded under Anglo-French pressure.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Czechia: From Great Moravia and the crown of Saint Wenceslas to the heart of Europe, by way of Hus, White Mountain and two peaceful revolutions.", terralore.co/country/CZE/chronicle#ev-1938-the-munich-agreement, claim TL:CZE:event:1938:the-munich-agreement, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: German annexation of the Sudetenland
claims.summary: Following the Munich Agreement, German forces occupied the Sudetenland, stripping Czechoslovakia of its border defences and around three million inhabitants in its German-speaking borderlands.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Czechia: From Great Moravia and the crown of Saint Wenceslas to the heart of Europe, by way of Hus, White Mountain and two peaceful revolutions.", terralore.co/country/CZE/chronicle#ev-1938-german-annexation-of-the-sudetenland, claim TL:CZE:event:1938:german-annexation-of-the-sudetenland, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Occupation and the Protectorate of Bohemia and Moravia
claims.summary: In breach of Munich, Germany occupied the Czech lands on 15 March 1939 and proclaimed the Protectorate of Bohemia and Moravia, while a separate Slovak state was set up under German control.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Czechia: From Great Moravia and the crown of Saint Wenceslas to the heart of Europe, by way of Hus, White Mountain and two peaceful revolutions.", terralore.co/country/CZE/chronicle#ev-1939-occupation-and-the-protectorate-of-bohemia-and, claim TL:CZE:event:1939:occupation-and-the-protectorate-of-bohemia-and, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Expulsion of the Sudeten Germans
claims.summary: Under the Benes decrees and Allied agreement at Potsdam, Czechoslovakia stripped the citizenship and property of its Germans and expelled some three million Sudeten Germans, the largest forced migration in the history of the Czech lands.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Czechia: From Great Moravia and the crown of Saint Wenceslas to the heart of Europe, by way of Hus, White Mountain and two peaceful revolutions.", terralore.co/country/CZE/chronicle#ev-1945-expulsion-of-the-sudeten-germans, claim TL:CZE:event:1945:expulsion-of-the-sudeten-germans, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Communist coup
claims.summary: In February 1948 the Communist Party seized full power in Czechoslovakia, ending postwar democracy and bringing the country firmly into the Soviet bloc for the next four decades.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Czechia: From Great Moravia and the crown of Saint Wenceslas to the heart of Europe, by way of Hus, White Mountain and two peaceful revolutions.", terralore.co/country/CZE/chronicle#ev-1948-communist-coup, claim TL:CZE:event:1948:communist-coup, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Prague Spring crushed by Warsaw Pact
claims.summary: Alexander Dubcek's reforms of 'socialism with a human face' were ended when roughly half a million Warsaw Pact troops, led by the Soviet Union, invaded Czechoslovakia in August 1968.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Czechia: From Great Moravia and the crown of Saint Wenceslas to the heart of Europe, by way of Hus, White Mountain and two peaceful revolutions.", terralore.co/country/CZE/chronicle#ev-1968-prague-spring-crushed-by-warsaw-pact, claim TL:CZE:event:1968:prague-spring-crushed-by-warsaw-pact, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: The Velvet Revolution
claims.summary: A suppressed student march in Prague on 17 November 1989 set off mass protests that toppled the communist regime within weeks; Vaclav Havel was elected president on 29 December.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Czechia: From Great Moravia and the crown of Saint Wenceslas to the heart of Europe, by way of Hus, White Mountain and two peaceful revolutions.", terralore.co/country/CZE/chronicle#ev-1989-the-velvet-revolution, claim TL:CZE:event:1989:the-velvet-revolution, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: The Velvet Divorce and birth of the Czech Republic
claims.summary: After a 1992 vote to divide, Czechoslovakia split peacefully on 1 January 1993 into the Czech Republic and Slovakia; the Czech Republic later joined NATO in 1999 and the EU in 2004.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Czechia: From Great Moravia and the crown of Saint Wenceslas to the heart of Europe, by way of Hus, White Mountain and two peaceful revolutions.", terralore.co/country/CZE/chronicle#ev-1993-the-velvet-divorce-and-birth-of-the-czech, claim TL:CZE:event:1993:the-velvet-divorce-and-birth-of-the-czech, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.
